content:
Facts: Son sued sister claiming father indirectly donated property-purchase money creating collation obligation; alleged father paid purchase price from joint parental account for property initially leased then decommissioned by public entity; sister counterclaimed alleging father transferred commercial-agent business to brother constituting gift infringing her legitimate portion.
Legal Framework: Articles 537, 542, 556, 737, 747, 750-751 Italian Civil Code (legitimate portions spouse-children; fictitious reunion; collation; donation valuation); case law on indirect donations (Cass. 10759/2019, 18725/2017 on direct cash donations via cheque).
Interpretive Issues: Scope of claim when introductory act alleges father-only donation but later pleadings reference parental donation; proof burden for indirect property donation through money provision; whether mortgage-installment payments by third party constitute indirect money donation or property donation; nullity of cash donations via cheque lacking prescribed form; collation mechanics when donations advance legitimate share; transferability of self-employment commercial-agent activity.
Principles Applied: Court cannot rule referencing two separate estates (father's, mother's) or combine estates as independent successions; reserved shares differ based on competing heirs (spouse-children versus children-only per Arts. 542, 537). Claim scope extracted from writ: property indirectly donated by father using joint-account money for price payment. Indirect donation through purchase-money provision requires documentary proof expressing specific donation-purchase link; partial price-coverage donations identified as ownership-percentage corresponding to donor-paid portion. Alleged December 2002 price-payment transactions unproven; account statements omitting described movements; no bank-draft request evidence. Mortgage installment payment (€21,609.72) via standing orders from joint account constitutes indirect money donation absent compensation-proof; third-party obligation-fulfillment out of generosity toward debtor creates indirect donation. Cash donations via cheque constitute direct donations; form-requirement exclusion applies only to causal contractual cases having inherent justifying cause, not abstract transactions (cheque issuance/endorsement) based on underlying relationship requiring substance/form compliance. Cheque-donation nullity for form defect enforceable in direct issuer-taker relationships; donation-as-typical-contract with binding form/mandatory rules precludes achieving immediate asset transfer via different forms. €45,000 cheque-donations void contributing to relictum formation. Donations favoring legitimate heirs presumed advances on legitimate share; Art. 737 collation obligation unless donor waives (effective within available-portion limits). Collation mechanism alone sufficient ensuring co-heir share-receipt without specific legitimate-portion protection when advances balance shares. Commercial-agent business non-transferable as self-employment; no proven financial advantage constituting generosity act. Damage-for-parental-care-failure claim rejected as generically formulated lacking damage-constituting elements.
